command: PYTHONPATH=plugin python -m memory.eval_recall --memory-dir <corpus> --index-dir <index> --hard-set <fixture> --telemetry-dir <dir> --ab HIPPO_GRAPH_PPR  (bm25_queries runs: same, under HIPPO_DISABLE_DENSE=1)

corpora.live_corpus: this repo's own .claude/memory (108 memories) with its project-local fixture .claude/memory/.audit-fixtures/recall_hard_set.yaml (16 single-hop rows, 0 multi-hop)
corpora.starter_packs: the CI corpus: plugin/assets packs seeded per tests/fixtures/recall_hard_set.yaml's header (22 memories) with that fixture (10 multi-hop, 22 single-hop)
corpora.live_corpus_grown: the same live corpus after its private fixture grew to 27 rows (16 single-hop + 11 multi-hop, added 2026-11-25 at the owner's request; 6 rows whose answer is one link from the memory the query leans on, 5 two links away; queries written before any recall run and not tuned). The corpus and fixture are private (gitignored), so these runs carry counts only: no queries, no memory names.

latency_interleaved_dense.method: one process, warm index, the hard-set queries x5 rounds, OFF/ON alternated per query (order flipped each round) so drift and cache effects hit both arms alike; the per-run latency_ms above runs the arms sequentially and is order-sensitive

reading: Live corpus with multi-hop rows (the decisive run): dense multi-hop recall 0.818 -> 0.727 (-1 row of 11), MRR 0.329 -> 0.297; single-hop unchanged (0.9375 / 0.760); BM25 queries: every delta 0. Starter packs: multi-hop MRR +0.046 at recall ceiling on a 10-pair graph. Net: on the graph where the walk should pay, it regressed by one row; the mechanism is the endorsement set's interaction with MMR, not the walk's reach (one 2-hop-ish row gained 8 -> 3). Latency: interleaved dense p50 +1.1 to +1.7 ms on a 15-20 ms call, p95 within noise; BM25-query p50 +0.2 to +0.3 ms.
recommendation: NO FLIP. The lane as built does not beat the 1-hop pull on the live graph (-1 multi-hop recall row of 11, single-hop flat). The design question it surfaced: how the walk's endorsed set should relate to GRA-1's (e.g. keep every 1-hop neighbor GRA-1 endorses and add the walk's top-mass nodes, so the walk can only add MMR/knee protection, never remove it). Any such variant must be judged on rows it was not designed against: these 11 are now in-sample.
per_row_diagnosis_live_grown_dense: Recall@10 rank of the expected memory, OFF -> ON, over the 11 multi-hop rows: 8 rows unchanged (6 hits, 2 misses under both); 1 row gained (rank 8 -> 3); 2 rows lost (rank 5 -> 7, and rank 2 -> outside the top 10). The lost top-10 hit was dropped as mmr_displaced: the walk endorses a different, smaller set than the 1-hop pull (10 vs 18 on that query), endorsed memories are exempt from MMR's diversity re-cut, so changing the endorsed set changed which candidates MMR protected and an organic rank-2 hit lost its slot.
